newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFins rise on US PPI, seen firming more.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins rise on US PPI, seen firming more.

text.p: MinFin bonds rose on Friday on heavy Western demand, boosted by a fall in U.S. producer prices, and dealers said they saw the bullish trend continuing.
"The market opened much higher, especially in tranches 4 and 5 on Thursday left-over orders from London," an Aljba-Alliance dealer said.

She said there was some profit-taking in the second half of the day, but after the U.S. government announced a 0.3 percent fall in the producer price index -- the first drop since October 1994 -- U.S. Treasuries started rising and MinFins followed.
Dealers forecast a strong and rising market in the next few days.
"We are dealing with a real investment boom, mainly from the U.S.," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said. "Risks connected to Russia have now diminished."
He said investors were encouraged by a strong performance in Russian shares and a fall in Treasury bill yields.
"Prices are now on a new level," Kovzharov said. "We are dealing with a very strong, steady trend."
